title: Places around town
source: User-provided workbook photo, manually transcribed; Word File German translations suggested separately

entries.description: A tall, narrow building, e.g. with a clock on top
A part of a town or city
A green place in town with grass and trees
A place where you can buy things
An open place in a town with buildings all around it
Water that flows through a town to the sea
A house, a school or an office, for example
A place where you can look at paintings
A big building with lots of stores inside
A road in a town with houses on both sides
You go over it to cross a river

entries.example: This stadium is home to the England national football team.
entries.description: A big place where people watch football matches

entries.example: The old Globe Theatre burnt down, but there's a new one.
entries.description: To be destroyed completely by fire

entries.example: This is an art gallery whose collection of modern art is one of the best in the world.
entries.description: A group of things someone has gathered, e.g. stamps

entries.example: It is where the British government meets.
entries.description: The people who run a country

entries.example: The government meets at the Houses of Parliament.
entries.description: The building in London where British laws are made

entries.example: If you want to avoid the long queues - book in advance.
entries.description: Before something happens; early

entries.example: A lot of people photograph these places in London.
entries.description: To take pictures with a camera

entries.example: You can watch a Shakespeare play at the Globe.
entries.description: A story that actors perform on stage

entries.example: It was built in 1078 as a castle, later it was a prison.
entries.description: A place where criminals are locked up

entries.example: They can raise the bridge for big ships.
entries.description: To lift something up

entries.example: The ravens should never leave the Tower of London.
entries.description: A large black bird

entries.example: Take a walk along the banks of the river.
entries.description: To go for a stroll on foot

entries.example: There was a round theatre here, where Shakespeare acted.
entries.description: A building where you can watch actors on a stage

entries.example: The 25-minute ride on the wheel gives you some of the best views of London.
entries.description: What you can see from a high place

entries.example: More than 3.5 million visitors take a ride on the wheel each year.
entries.description: Someone who comes to see a place or a person

entries.example: Let's throw a thrilling party on Thursday.
entries.description: Very exciting

entries.example: The Great Plague killed approximately 100,000 people in London.
entries.description: About, roughly; not exactly

entries.example: Usual symptoms were fever and coughing up blood.
entries.description: To push air out of your throat noisily when you are ill

entries.example: The Great Plague was a cruel killer.
entries.description: Very unkind; happy to hurt others

entries.example: The streets were empty. There were no people.
entries.description: With nothing or nobody inside

entries.example: If you had the Plague, you also had fever.
entries.description: When your body is too hot because you are ill

entries.example: Many people didn't report their symptoms.
entries.description: To tell someone officially what happened

entries.example: There's a long path, a lake and lots of trees.
entries.description: A narrow way for walking, e.g. through a forest

entries.example: What I loved most was the spectacular light show.
entries.description: Amazing and very impressive to look at

entries.example: Madame Tussauds has been a popular tourist attraction for many years.
entries.description: A famous place that many travellers want to see

entries.example: You can experience one of the many interactive attractions.
entries.description: To have something happen to you and feel it

entries.example: There's a lot of traffic on the street. It's very noisy.
entries.description: All the cars and buses on the roads

entries.example: London is very multicultural.
entries.description: With people from many different countries and backgrounds

entries.example: We signed a contract.
entries.description: A written agreement that people put their names on

entries.example: I should be helping Dad to lead a healthier lifestyle.
entries.description: To guide others or be in charge of them

entries.example: I want to eat less sugar.
entries.description: Sweet white stuff you can put in tea

entries.example: My other job earns me £10 a week.
entries.description: To get paid for your work

entries.example: I need to save up money for our new project.
entries.description: To keep money so you can buy something later

entries.example: He agreed and signed the contract.
entries.description: To write your name on a document
